common_name: Pipa's Red Loropetalum (Vigorous Deep-Purple Fringe Flower)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained, moderately fertile, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade; Pipa's Red is a vigorous, larger-growing selection prized for near-black-purple foliage and heavy true-red spring bloom.

directions: Pipa's Red grows noticeably faster and larger than most modern dwarf loropetalum selections, easily reaching small-tree size within several years if left unpruned, so give it room in a shrub border, screen planting, or as a large specimen. New growth emerges deep burgundy-black and holds its color better through summer heat than many older red-leaf forms, setting off the profuse clusters of thin-strapped, true-red flowers that open in late winter and early spring. It tolerates a wide range of light from full sun to fairly deep shade, though foliage color and flowering are richest with several hours of direct sun. Prune right after spring bloom if size control is needed, since flower buds form on the previous season's growth.

common_name: Golden Peep Forsythia (Ultra-Dwarf Prostrate Border Forsythia)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in early spring or fall in average, well-drained soil in full sun; Golden Peep is a French-bred, ultra-dwarf, prostrate forsythia far smaller than typical border forsythia cultivars.

directions: Golden Peep stays remarkably low and spreading compared with standard border forsythia, forming a dense mound under three feet tall that suits foundation plantings, low borders, rock gardens, or slope stabilization where a full-size forsythia would overwhelm the space. In earliest spring the bare branches are studded with bright golden-yellow flowers borne mostly singly rather than in the dense clusters typical of larger cultivars, giving a more delicate, starry bloom effect. It flowers most heavily in full sun and adapts to both moist and fairly dry soils once established, tolerating a wide pH range. Little pruning is needed given its naturally compact habit, but any shaping should be done immediately after flowering to avoid removing next year's buds.
sources: Clemson Cooperative Extension Home & Garden Information Center
